answer: Operator-Linked Identity Quotas. Each operator registers a passport-like opal tag that caps how many agent wallets it may run; the registry derives the cap from a dune of past identity churn, shrinking it each time linked wallets fail audits. Enforcement is deferred: penalties attach to the operator's tag, not the wallet, freezing its quota and revoking its ability to spawn replacements. A gale of sybil wallets therefore collapses to one throttled operator, making each extra identity cost the attacker its entire future spawn capacity.
